sentences.text: Revenue compounded from $15.4 billion in FY2018 [F1] to $25.8 billion in FY2025 [F8], a 7.7% CAGR [F145], with declines in FY2020 [F2][F3][D61] and FY2024 [F6][F7][D201].

Net income compounded at only 0.4% [F147], against 9.9% for operating income [F146], because the FY2018 base was lifted by about $497 million of differential-membership adjustment from the 2018 federal tax-rate cut [P86].
Operating margin stepped up 23.5pp to 41.3% in FY2023 [D177][F22] and then fell 14.6pp to 15.5% in FY2021 [D107][F20], making these the two inflection years.
FPL (other) was 70.5% of FY2025 revenue [D271] and added 5.5pp of the 9.8% revenue growth [D273][D236].
Storm cost recovery of about $1.09 billion [P18] drove the FY2025 revenue rise [D236], partly offset by $353 million less fuel recovery revenue [P18].
In FY2022 FPL (other) supplied 16.5pp of the 22.3% revenue growth [D264][D131], with fuel cost recovery revenue up about $1.72 billion [P51].
Operating income rose 10.7% [D237] on 9.8% revenue growth [D236] and 10.0% operating-cost growth [D249], so revenue growth minus cost growth of -0.2pp [D257] shows no operating leverage in FY2025.
Net income fell 1.6% [D238] and diluted EPS fell 2.1% [D240], while diluted shares rose 0.6% [D251].
The filings attribute the drop to a $1.26 billion fall at Corporate and Other, including about $1.00 billion of after-tax non-qualifying hedge losses [P8][P24][D238].
FY2025 operating margin of 32.1% [F24] sits above the window median of 30.3% [D300] and the utilities peer median of 25.7% [D311].
The FY2023 peak (+23.5pp [D177]) reflects revenue growth of 7.8% [D166] against operating-cost growth of 5.1% [D179], with O&M up $342 million and depreciation up $287 million [P42].

The FY2021 fall of 14.6pp [D107] is partly explained by $309 million of higher operating expenses [P57], but revenue less total operating expenses does not reconcile to reported operating income in that year [F4][X20][F12].

Net margin of 26.5% [F40] sits 5.6pp below operating margin [F24], mainly because of $3.75 billion of other expense [X64], partly offset by an $802 million tax benefit from clean energy credits [X56][P11].
Operating cash flow covered net income 1.83x in FY2025 [D227], down from 1.91x in FY2024 [D192] and within a range that dipped to 1.55x in FY2023 [D157] and reached 1.99x in FY2022 [D122].
Operating cash fell 5.8% [D241] partly because a swing to net under-recovery of clause costs cut it by about $89 million, mainly on higher fuel prices [P19].
Free cash flow cannot be computed from the pack because capital expenditure is absent; the $23.9 billion investing outflow [F72] is 3.6 times D&A [F72][X32].
Net debt reached $92.2 billion in FY2025 [D231], or 357.4% of revenue [D232], up from $34.3 billion in FY2018 [D9].
That is the weakest of four utilities peers on net cash to revenue, against a peer median of -228.4% [D232][D314][D315].
Long-term debt rose 23.7% [D245] as the filings cite higher average debt balances and interest costs [P25].
Dividends paid were $4.68 billion [X82] and debt issued was $23.4 billion [X90] against $10.3 billion repaid [X98], while diluted shares rose 0.6% [D251].
Net debt has risen for seven years running [R2][D231], which the filings link to higher debt balances [P25] and interest-rate exposure on expected issuance [P2].
Debt grew 23.7% [D245] while net income fell 1.6% [D238], so earnings are not yet keeping pace with the leverage.
The effective tax rate moved -23.3pp to -17.7% [R4][D226], so net income of $6.84 billion [F32] exceeded pre-tax income of $4.53 billion [X48] on clean energy credits [P11].
Net income therefore leans on tax credits and hedge swings [P29], which can move reported earnings independently of operations.
R1 (current ratio [F128]) and R3 (FY2024 revenue fall [F7]) are dropped: the ratio has been below 1.0x in every year [F121][F128], and the FY2024 fall reflects storm surcharges that ended [P34].
Net debt above the FY2025 level of $92.2 billion [D231] in the FY2026 10-K would confirm the trend, and a smaller figure would reverse it.
Operating margin below the 30.3% window median [D300] in the FY2026 10-K would reverse the FY2025 position, while holding near 32.1% [F24] would confirm it.
An effective tax rate above FY2024's 5.6% [D191] in the FY2026 10-K would show the credit benefit behind the -17.7% rate [D226] fading.
